newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 6.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima said yesterday in Vienna while meeting with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus that the EU finds the Czech import deposit unfavourable and it is causing definite complications for Austrian businesses.

- Vice-governer of the central bank, Pavel Kysilka, said yesterday that a decrease in interest rates is not currently on the agenda. He added that the bank is also not considering extending the fluctuation band for the crown beyond the current 7.5 percent above and below parity.
- Today, economic ministers should discuss division of tax payments for the next year.
- Health Minister Jan Strasky gave a time period of one month to revise the new list of low-risk health operations which should be valid from July 1 for health insurance companies.

LIDOVE NOVINY - A petition containing more than 66,000 signatures was given to the cabinet yesterday by the chairman of the school workers' union, Jaroslav Rossler. Those signed protest against increasing requirements and low wages for teachers.

- Total wage increases for Czech Railways will be 12 percent this year, although the original estimate was 13.7 percent and the increase guaranteed to employees is 17.2 percent. General director Vladimir Sosna said they will reach the guaranteed increase by laying off 5,200 workers.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The management of Motol Hospital in Prague will put pressure on the doctors' union to cover financial losses caused by the longest strike of doctors and nurses so far. The strike has already reached its fifth day.

- The main point on the agenda of today's general meeting of shareholders of Poldi Steel is to vote on new members of Poldi's supervisory council and probably oust former owner Vladimir Stehlik from his post as council chairman.
- The rate of increase in money supplies slowed down further in February and reached 6.2 percent year-on-year after 7.1 percent in January.
- Moravskoslezske Teplarny increased its stake in Teplarny Karvina to 49.97 percent from 27.
- Tabak had net profits last year of 1.6 billion crowns, about 204 million less than in 1995.
- Slovakia wants to put quotas in effect for imports of Czech beer, according to Slovak Agriculture Minister Peter Baco.

- The Japanese investment bank Nomura International called on the Czech cabinet yesterday not to prolong the privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka because of the alleged crimes of two members of its management.

PRAVO - The cabinet's decision on the tender for Aero Vodochody should be announced on Wednesday. Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy should present the cabinet's evaluation of the relevant committee's proposal.

- According to preliminary calculations from the Trade Ministry the Czech Republic changed from creditor to debtor in 1996. Its gross debts increased last year by $3.9 billion dollars and reached $20.4 billion at the end of the year. Foreign debts make up 39 percent of the country's GDP.
- During the first quarter of this year, railway passenger transport declined by 10 percent compared to the same time the year before. In freight transport, there was a decrease of 7.2 percent.
- Plzensky Prazdroj brewery is planning to request the Industry and Trade Ministry for an exemption from import deposits on cans and hop extract.
